constraints.name: Employee data protection
constraints.rationale_summary: Processing employee names and financial claim data is a standard obligation for any UK internal system — not a feasibility blocker.
constraints.reasoning: Identified via the cross-domain regulator index as the applicable body/framework for any system processing employee personal data; classified Green since this is a routine, not novel, obligation.

constraints.name: Financial record retention
constraints.rationale_summary: Approval/claim records are accounting records requiring statutory minimum retention; allowing early deletion would create a compliance gap.
constraints.mitigation_summary: Design the tool so claim/approval records cannot be deleted before the statutory retention period elapses, and are exportable for audit.
constraints.reasoning: Not covered by either attached KB (this example falls outside the food domain); resolved via tool-L1-regulatory-db-lookup instead. Classified as an ongoing duty per the scenario rules, not a one-off setup step.

constraints.name: Accessibility of the internal interface

citation.regulation: Equality Act 2010, s.20 (duty to make reasonable adjustments)

constraints.rationale_summary: An internal tool all staff must use carries a reasonable-adjustments duty; standard WCAG-aligned design discharges it.
constraints.reasoning: Swept under the accessibility category. Not a blocker for an internal tool where accessible design is a routine build decision, so Green rather than Amber.

overall_status.rationale_summary: CON-02 (financial record retention) is the worst constraint at Amber, with a concrete, precedented mitigation. No Red item exists.

categories_not_applicable.category: Intellectual property and third-party data licensing

components.reasoning: overall_status Amber with the single Amber constraint carrying a concrete, precedented design mitigation, and no Red or legal-review item. Scores at the top of the 7-8 band.

components.reasoning: The problem names who suffers it (Finance and claimants), how it is felt today (re-keying, no status visibility), and a tightly bounded internal scope the regulatory perimeter could be drawn around.
